purpose: Teach: 瓩/屬/璽/錣/註/楼/个/北村

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、押収物の重量、瓩、つまりキロ表示を確認されますね
lines.en: The police do check the weight of seized items in kilograms, don't they?
lines.style: Matter-of-fact, steady rhythm. Observational tone—stating what he knows to be true. Slight upward lilt at the end, inviting confirmation rather than challenging.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、旧字「屬」、つまり属の表記の古文書も鑑定されますね
lines.en: And they also authenticate old documents with the classical character form for 'belong,' I imagine?
lines.style: Same steady, cooperative pace. Building naturally on the previous thought. Tone remains warm and interested, not interrogative.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、官印、つまり璽の偽造事件にも対応されますね
lines.en: They handle forgery cases involving official seals too, correct?
lines.style: Continuing smoothly. Conversational, not testing. Breath control even—he's genuinely walking through a list of responsibilities with respect.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、武具の錣、つまり兜部位の盗難事件も捜査されますね
lines.en: And theft investigations involving armor parts—the protective face guard of helmets and such—those fall under your purview as well?
lines.style: Slight warmth entering now. The specificity suggests admiration for the breadth of their work. Pace remains unhurried, voice stays level.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、調書の註、つまり註記を慎重に書かれますね
lines.en: I imagine the annotations in official statements are written with particular care, aren't they?
lines.style: Gentle shift in tone—almost tender now. Less listing, more genuine interest in the detail and precision required. Soft finish.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、高層楼、つまり高楼での捜査も担当されますね
lines.en: And investigations in high-rise buildings—that's part of your work too?
lines.style: Returning to straightforward curiosity. No change in pace or warmth, but the question feels genuinely interested in their world.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、旧表記の个、つまり個の証拠点数を整理されますね
lines.en: I suppose you have to carefully organize the evidence counts, even when using older numerical notation?
lines.style: Slight appreciation in the voice now. Acknowledging the methodical work behind the scenes. Warm but professional.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、参考人の北村さんから事情を、警察、丁寧に聴かれますね
lines.en: And you listen carefully to witnesses like Kitamura-san when gathering their statements, don't you?
lines.style: Warmer, more personal. The shift from abstract to a specific name softens the tone. Genuine regard for the care taken. Quiet confidence at the close.
